proof_summary: For primes \(p,q\) with different final digits and \(pq\le150\), if neither divides \(d\), then \(d\) is invertible modulo \(pq\), so some \(0\le i<150\) makes \(a+id\) divisible by both primes, a contradiction; hence \(p\mid d\) or \(q\mid d\). Applying this to a finite set of prime pairs and using \(d\le2025\) successively forces \(2,3,5,7,11\mid d\), so \(2310\mid d\), contradicting the bound.
